routes.name: East Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Colorado's second highest peak follows a well-maintained trail from the Mount Massive trailhead through dense forest before emerging above treeline onto broad, gentle slopes. The upper mountain is a long ridge walk with stunning views of the Sawatch Range. Navigation can be tricky in fog due to the expansive summit plateau.
routes.summary: Standard hiking route up Colorado's second highest peak via gentle eastern slopes.
routes.safetyNotes: The summit ridge is long and exposed. Start early to avoid afternoon thunderstorms. The broad plateau makes navigation difficult in whiteout conditions.

tips.content: Start before sunrise to avoid afternoon lightning on the exposed summit ridge.
Carry extra water as there are no reliable sources above treeline.
Use GPS or a map to stay on route across the featureless upper plateau.

gear.notes: Helpful on the long approach and descent
Afternoon storms are common above treeline
Useful for navigation on the broad summit plateau

reviews.title: Long but rewarding
reviews.body: A beautiful hike with incredible views from the summit. The trail is well-maintained through the forest but gets faint above treeline. Budget extra time for the long ridge walk.

reviews.title: Stunning Sawatch views
reviews.body: One of the best summit panoramas in Colorado. The route is straightforward but don't underestimate the distance. I could see Elbert, La Plata, and dozens of other peaks from the top.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, some wind, early August

routes.name: Southwest Slopes
routes.description: An alternate route that approaches Mount Massive from the southwest via Halfmoon Creek. This route sees fewer hikers than the standard East Slopes and offers a different perspective of the mountain. The trail climbs through aspen groves before reaching alpine tundra and the long summit ridge.
routes.summary: Less-traveled alternate route approaching from the southwest via Halfmoon Creek.
routes.safetyNotes: Trail can be faint in the upper basin. Afternoon storms build quickly on this side of the mountain. Carry navigation tools.

tips.content: This route is less crowded than the East Slopes and offers more solitude.
The trail becomes faint above treeline; look for cairns to stay on route.

gear.notes: Trail is faint in the upper basin
Extended exposure above treeline

reviews.title: Great alternative to the crowded east side
reviews.body: Had the mountain nearly to myself on a Saturday. The approach through the aspens is beautiful in fall. Route finding above treeline requires attention.
reviews.conditions: Clear skies, late September, aspens turning

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Colorado's third highest peak begins at the North Cottonwood trailhead and follows the Horn Fork Basin trail. After crossing timberline, the route ascends moderate grassy slopes to the summit. This is the most popular and straightforward way up Mount Harvard.
routes.summary: Standard route ascending grassy slopes from Horn Fork Basin to Colorado's third highest summit.
routes.safetyNotes: North Cottonwood Creek crossing can be dangerous during spring runoff. The upper slopes are exposed to lightning. Start early.

tips.content: An early start is essential as the upper slopes are completely exposed to afternoon storms.
The creek crossing early in the hike can be challenging during snowmelt season.
Consider combining with Mount Columbia for a challenging double summit day.

gear.notes: Helpful for stream crossings and the long descent
Several stream crossings on the approach
Extended sun exposure above treeline

reviews.title: A classic Colorado 14er
reviews.body: Straightforward route with stunning views. The Horn Fork Basin is beautiful and the summit views stretch forever. Long day but very manageable for fit hikers.

reviews.title: Long approach but worth it
reviews.body: The approach through the forest feels long but the alpine scenery above treeline is spectacular. Summit views of the Collegiate Peaks are incredible.

routes.name: North Slopes
routes.description: A less-traveled approach to Mount Harvard from the north, starting near the Pine Creek trailhead. This route climbs through a scenic basin on the north side of the peak and is often combined with Mount Columbia. The terrain is moderate but the route is longer and more remote.
routes.summary: Longer northern approach often combined with a Mount Columbia summit attempt.
routes.safetyNotes: This is a long and remote route. Ensure you have adequate supplies and navigation skills. Cell service is unreliable.

tips.content: Best done as part of a Harvard-Columbia combo to maximize the long approach.
Bring extra food and water for the longer route distance.

gear.notes: Remote terrain with faint trails
Long day with limited water sources above treeline

reviews.title: Remote and beautiful
reviews.body: Fewer people than the south side. The basin approach is stunning and the Harvard-Columbia combo makes for an epic day. Be prepared for a very long outing.

routes.name: Northwest Face
routes.description: The standard hiking route on Blanca Peak ascends the northwest face from the Lake Como road approach. After navigating the notoriously rough 4WD road (or hiking it), the route follows a well-cairned path up moderate talus and scree slopes to the summit. This is the most popular route on Blanca.
routes.summary: Standard route up the northwest face with a notorious 4WD road approach.
routes.safetyNotes: The Lake Como road is one of the roughest in Colorado and has damaged many vehicles. Most hikers walk the road, adding significant distance. Upper mountain has loose rock.

tips.content: Unless you have a highly capable 4WD vehicle, plan to hike the road which adds about 6 miles round trip.
Consider camping at Lake Como to break the long day into two shorter days.
Stay on the cairned route to avoid the worst of the loose scree.

gear.notes: Recommended for loose rock on upper mountain
Helpful for scree and talus sections
Useful for the long road walk and descent

reviews.title: Beautiful peak, brutal approach
reviews.body: The summit views are among the best in Colorado but the approach is punishing. Walking the 4WD road adds hours. Consider backpacking to Lake Como.
reviews.conditions: Hot and sunny, loose scree, mid-July

reviews.title: Epic summit with a Sangre de Cristo panorama
reviews.body: Camped at Lake Como which made the summit day very manageable. The NW face route is straightforward but tedious on scree. Views of the Great Sand Dunes from the summit are incredible.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, early August

routes.name: Lake Como Approach
routes.description: This variation of the Blanca Peak route focuses on the direct approach from Lake Como, climbing the Blanca-Little Bear saddle before ascending the upper northwest face. It offers a slightly different perspective than the standard NW face route and can be combined with Little Bear Peak for experienced climbers.
routes.summary: Direct approach from Lake Como with options to combine with Little Bear Peak.
routes.safetyNotes: Distances assume you have driven or camped at Lake Como. Some sections near the saddle involve mild exposure. Rockfall danger increases with other parties above.

tips.content: Camp at Lake Como the night before for an early alpine start.
If combining with Little Bear, assess conditions carefully as the connecting ridge is Class 4.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall protection on the upper mountain
For overnight at Lake Como

reviews.title: Camping at Lake Como is the way to go
reviews.body: Made this into a two-day trip by camping at the lake. The approach from camp is reasonable and the upper mountain is exciting scrambling. Stunning views of Little Bear.
reviews.conditions: Cool morning, clear skies, early August

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on La Plata Peak ascends the northwest ridge from the La Plata Gulch trailhead on Highway 82. The trail climbs steeply through forest before reaching the alpine ridge which leads directly to the summit. This is a well-traveled and straightforward route.
routes.summary: Standard route climbing the northwest ridge from Highway 82.
routes.safetyNotes: The upper ridge is exposed to weather. The trail is steep in places, especially the initial climb through the forest. Start early to avoid storms.

tips.content: The trailhead parking area fills up quickly on weekends; arrive early.
The trail is steep from the start, so pace yourself for the long day.
Carry extra layers as the ridge can be windy even on calm days.

gear.notes: Very helpful on the steep descent
Ridge is often windy
Trail is well-defined but map is good backup

reviews.title: Steep but scenic
reviews.body: A solid Class 2 hike with great views of the Sawatch Range. The trail is relentlessly steep in the lower section but the ridge walk above treeline is beautiful.

reviews.title: Fifth highest but underrated
reviews.body: La Plata doesn't get the attention of its neighbors but the summit views are excellent. The northwest ridge is a straightforward and enjoyable route.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.description: An alternative approach to La Plata Peak from the south, this route climbs the southwest ridge and offers a less crowded experience. The trail is less well-defined than the standard route but the terrain is moderate. Good route-finding skills are helpful above treeline.
routes.summary: Less-crowded alternate route up the southwest ridge with moderate terrain.
routes.safetyNotes: Trail is less defined above treeline. Carry navigation tools and pay attention to weather.

tips.content: This route sees far fewer hikers, making it a better choice for solitude seekers.
Mark your route with GPS on the ascent to make the descent easier.

gear.notes: Trail is faint in the upper section
Helpful on loose terrain

reviews.title: Peaceful alternative
reviews.body: Had the entire route to myself on a Saturday. The trail disappears above treeline but the ridge is easy to follow with a GPS. Beautiful views into the valley.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: The easiest route on Uncompahgre Peak and one of the simplest 14er climbs in Colorado. The trail starts at Nellie Creek trailhead and follows a well-maintained path to the broad south ridge, which leads gently to the summit. This is an excellent first 14er for beginners.
routes.summary: One of the easiest 14er routes in Colorado, following a gentle trail up the south ridge.
routes.safetyNotes: Though this is an easy route, altitude sickness can still be a concern. The upper ridge is exposed to lightning. Start early.

tips.content: This is an excellent first 14er for beginners due to the moderate distance and elevation gain.
The Nellie Creek road requires high clearance but not necessarily 4WD in dry conditions.
Bring binoculars to enjoy the panoramic views of the San Juan Mountains.

gear.notes: Helpful but not necessary on this gentle trail
Afternoon storms common in the San Juans
Minimal shade above treeline

reviews.title: Perfect first 14er
reviews.body: Did this as my first 14er and it was perfect. The trail is clear, the grade is moderate, and the views from the summit are incredible. Highly recommend for beginners.

reviews.title: Easy but still beautiful
reviews.body: Don't let the easy rating fool you into thinking it's boring. The San Juan views from the summit are some of the best in the state. Just a lovely day hike.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds building by noon, early August

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: An alternative approach to Uncompahgre Peak from the west that offers more solitude and slightly more challenging terrain than the standard South Ridge. The route climbs through a scenic basin before reaching the upper west face, where moderate scree leads to the summit.
routes.summary: Less-traveled western approach with moderate scree climbing and more solitude.
routes.safetyNotes: The west face has loose scree that requires careful footing. This route is less traveled and trail markings may be sparse.

tips.content: This route offers more solitude than the popular South Ridge approach.
Gaiters are recommended for the scree sections on the upper face.

gear.notes: Keeps scree out of boots on the upper face
Trail markings sparse on this route

reviews.title: Nice alternative for solitude
reviews.body: Chose this route to avoid the crowds on the south ridge and was not disappointed. The scree on the upper face is tedious but the basin approach is beautiful.

routes.name: South Face/Red Couloir
routes.description: The standard route on Crestone Peak ascends the south face via the Red Couloir, a prominent gully filled with loose red rock. The approach from the South Colony Lakes trailhead is long and the upper couloir involves sustained Class 3 scrambling with considerable exposure. This is one of the more challenging standard 14er routes in Colorado.
routes.summary: Challenging Class 3 route up the prominent Red Couloir on the south face.
routes.safetyNotes: The Red Couloir has serious rockfall danger, especially with parties above. Wear a helmet at all times in the couloir. The rock is notoriously loose. Start very early to minimize rockfall from other parties.

tips.content: Camp at South Colony Lakes to allow an early alpine start for this demanding route.
Climb early when the couloir rock is more frozen and stable, reducing rockfall risk.
Consider combining with Crestone Needle if you are an experienced scrambler.

gear.notes: Absolutely essential for rockfall protection in the couloir
Ankle support critical on loose terrain
Helpful for route finding on the approach

reviews.title: Demanding but incredible
reviews.body: This route earns its reputation. The Red Couloir is steep, loose, and exposed. But the summit views are among the best in Colorado. Helmet is mandatory.
reviews.conditions: Clear and cold, frost on rock early morning, late July

reviews.title: Serious route on a serious mountain
reviews.body: Do not underestimate Crestone Peak. The couloir rock is extremely loose and rockfall is a constant concern. Rewarding summit but you earn every foot of elevation.
reviews.conditions: Calm morning, clouds by noon, early August

routes.name: Northwest Couloir
routes.description: An alternate route on Crestone Peak that approaches from the northwest. This couloir offers a different challenge than the Red Couloir with slightly more solid rock in some sections. The approach is longer but the route sees fewer climbers, reducing rockfall danger from other parties.
routes.summary: Alternate Class 3 couloir approach from the northwest with fewer crowds.
routes.safetyNotes: Route finding can be challenging. The couloir has sections of loose rock requiring a helmet. Longer approach means a longer day.

tips.content: This route has less rockfall danger from other parties due to lower traffic.
Study the route description carefully before attempting as markers can be sparse.

gear.notes: Essential for loose rock sections
Route finding is complex on this approach

reviews.title: Less crowded alternative
reviews.body: Chose the NW couloir to avoid the crowded Red Couloir and was glad I did. Still serious scrambling but felt safer with fewer parties above sending rocks down.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cool, early morning start from camp, mid-August

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Lincoln follows the well-maintained trail from Kite Lake up gentle alpine tundra to the broad summit. This is one of the easiest 14er routes in Colorado and is frequently combined with nearby peaks Democrat, Cameron, and Bross in the popular Decalibron loop.
routes.summary: Easy trail from Kite Lake making this one of the simplest 14er routes in Colorado.
routes.safetyNotes: Despite the easy terrain, altitude can still cause problems. The ridge is exposed to wind and lightning. Start early if combining with other peaks.

tips.content: Combine with Democrat, Cameron, and Bross for the popular Decalibron loop.
Kite Lake trailhead fills up very quickly on weekends; arrive by 5 AM.
Start with Democrat and traverse to Cameron, Lincoln, then Bross for the most efficient loop.

gear.notes: Ridges can be very windy
Entirely above treeline with no shade
Helpful on the talus sections

reviews.title: Great peak for the Decalibron
reviews.body: Did Lincoln as part of the Decalibron loop and it was a fantastic day. The summit offers great views and the traverse is enjoyable. Easy terrain throughout.

reviews.title: Easy and scenic
reviews.body: A straightforward hike to a beautiful summit. Combined with Democrat and Cameron for three 14ers in one day. Parking at Kite Lake was full by 6 AM on a Saturday.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, moderate wind, late July

routes.name: Democrat-Lincoln Traverse
routes.description: This traverse connects Mount Democrat to Mount Lincoln via Mount Cameron, following gentle ridgeline trails above 14000 feet. The route is part of the famous Decalibron loop and stays entirely above treeline on well-worn trails. Outstanding views of the Mosquito and Tenmile Ranges throughout.
routes.summary: Scenic ridgeline traverse connecting Democrat to Lincoln via Cameron above 14000 feet.
routes.safetyNotes: The entire traverse is above treeline with no shelter from storms. Extended time at extreme altitude. Turn back if weather deteriorates.

tips.content: Start with Democrat first, then traverse to Cameron and Lincoln for the best flow.
Bring plenty of water and snacks for the extended time above 14000 feet.

gear.notes: No shelter above treeline on the traverse
No water sources on the ridgeline

reviews.title: Three 14ers in one shot
reviews.body: What a deal! Three 14ers in a single moderate hike. The ridge walking is spectacular and the terrain is easy. Just watch the weather on the exposed ridgeline.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds building by 11 AM, early August

routes.name: North Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Grays Peak is one of the most popular 14er hikes in Colorado, following a well-maintained trail from the Stevens Gulch trailhead. The trail gradually ascends switchbacks to the broad summit. Grays is typically combined with neighboring Torreys Peak for a two-summit day.
routes.summary: One of the most popular 14er routes in Colorado with a well-maintained trail.
routes.safetyNotes: Very popular trail that can be crowded on weekends. Start early to avoid parking issues and afternoon storms.

tips.content: Combine with Torreys Peak by traversing the connecting ridge for two 14ers in one day.
The trailhead lot fills extremely fast on summer weekends; arrive before sunrise.
This is an excellent first 14er due to the well-maintained trail and moderate difficulty.

gear.notes: Afternoon thunderstorms are very common
Helpful on the switchbacks and descent
Above treeline for most of the hike

reviews.title: Classic Colorado 14er combo
reviews.body: Did Grays and Torreys together for a perfect day. The trail is excellent and the views are stunning. Parking was full by 6:30 AM on a Saturday so get there early.

reviews.title: Great first 14er
reviews.body: Perfect introduction to 14er hiking. The trail is well-marked and the grade is moderate. Definitely plan to do Torreys as well while you're up there.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, light wind, late July

routes.name: West Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Antero follows a rough 4WD road and trail from the Baldwin Creek area up the western slopes. Mount Antero is famous for its gem-quality aquamarine crystals, and many hikers combine the climb with mineral collecting. The route is straightforward but the approach road requires high clearance.
routes.summary: Standard route following 4WD roads and trails up the gem-rich western slopes.
routes.safetyNotes: The access road is very rough and damages vehicles regularly. High clearance 4WD recommended. Upper slopes are exposed to lightning.

tips.content: Mount Antero is famous for aquamarine crystals; bring a rock hammer if you want to collect.
The 4WD road shortens the hike considerably if your vehicle can handle it.
The road can be driven part way even without 4WD to shorten the approach.

gear.notes: For mineral collecting on the slopes
Exposed summit area with frequent afternoon storms
Helpful on loose talus slopes

reviews.title: Gem hunting on a 14er
reviews.body: Where else can you bag a 14er and hunt for aquamarine crystals? The route is straightforward but the 4WD road is rough. Found some nice specimens on the upper slopes.

reviews.title: Unique among 14ers
reviews.body: The mineral deposits make this peak unlike any other 14er. The hike itself is moderate and the views of the Sawatch Range are excellent. Drive as far as you can to shorten the walk.

routes.name: Baldwin Gulch
routes.description: An alternate approach to Mount Antero via Baldwin Gulch from the southeast. This route is longer but avoids the rough 4WD road of the standard west slopes route. The trail follows Baldwin Creek before climbing to the upper slopes and joining the standard route near the summit.
routes.summary: Longer alternate approach via Baldwin Gulch avoiding the rough 4WD road.
routes.safetyNotes: Longer route but with better road access. Stream crossings can be difficult during spring runoff.

tips.content: This route has better road access for passenger vehicles compared to the standard west slopes.
The creek crossings are easier later in summer after snowmelt subsides.

gear.notes: Stream crossings on the approach
Trail can be faint in the upper gulch

reviews.title: Better access than the standard route
reviews.body: Chose this route because my car couldn't handle the west slopes road. Longer but the approach through Baldwin Gulch is pleasant and the trail is in good shape.

routes.name: Kelso Ridge
routes.description: Kelso Ridge is a classic Colorado scramble that ascends the dramatic southwest ridge of Torreys Peak. The route features sustained Class 3 scrambling on generally solid rock with significant exposure. It is one of the most popular scrambling routes on any Colorado 14er and offers a much more exciting alternative to the standard hiking trail.
routes.summary: Classic and popular Class 3 scramble up the dramatic southwest ridge.
routes.safetyNotes: Sustained exposure on the ridge. The rock is generally solid but some loose sections exist. Retreat is difficult once committed to the ridge. Do not attempt in wet or stormy conditions.

tips.content: This is an excellent introduction to alpine ridge scrambling in Colorado.
Start very early as the ridge is fully exposed to lightning with no easy retreat.
Descend via the standard south slopes trail rather than down-climbing the ridge.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall protection on the ridge
Helpful for the sustained hand-over-hand scrambling
Ridge is extremely exposed to weather

reviews.title: Best scramble in the Front Range
reviews.body: Kelso Ridge is an absolute classic. The scrambling is fun, the exposure is exciting, and the rock is mostly solid. One of my favorite routes in Colorado.
reviews.conditions: Clear and calm, early morning start, mid-July

reviews.title: Thrilling ridge scramble
reviews.body: Great step up from hiking for those wanting to try scrambling. The exposure is real but manageable. Descended the standard trail which was a nice contrast to the ridge.

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.description: The standard hiking route on Torreys Peak from the Stevens Gulch trailhead. Most hikers combine this with Grays Peak by traversing the connecting saddle. The trail is well-maintained and follows gentle switchbacks to the summit. This is one of the most popular 14er hikes near Denver.
routes.summary: Standard hiking trail typically combined with Grays Peak for a two-summit day.
routes.safetyNotes: Very popular trail. Start early for parking and to avoid storms. The Grays-Torreys saddle can be windy.

tips.content: Most efficient to summit Grays first, then traverse to Torreys and descend directly.
The saddle between Grays and Torreys can be very windy; bring a wind layer.

gear.notes: Saddle between Grays and Torreys is notoriously windy
Helpful on the descent

reviews.title: Perfect combo with Grays
reviews.body: Did Grays and Torreys together for an amazing day. The traverse between them is easy and scenic. Torreys summit has great views up and down the Continental Divide.
reviews.conditions: Bluebird day, calm winds, early July

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Castle Peak ascends the northeast ridge from the Montezuma Mine area near Ashcroft. The trail crosses Conundrum Creek before climbing steeply through willows and talus to the ridgeline. The final push involves moderate scrambling on loose rock to reach the pointed summit.
routes.summary: Standard route ascending the northeast ridge with moderate scrambling near the summit.
routes.safetyNotes: Conundrum Creek crossing can be tricky during high water. The upper ridge has loose rock. Summit block requires careful scrambling.

tips.content: The trail through the willows below the ridge can be wet and overgrown early in summer.
Castle and Conundrum Peaks can be combined by traversing the connecting ridge.
The final summit push looks intimidating but goes at moderate Class 2.

gear.notes: Helpful for wet willows and talus
Recommended for loose rock on the upper ridge
Useful for creek crossing and descent

reviews.title: Beautiful but remote
reviews.body: Castle Peak is worth the drive to the trailhead. The route is straightforward but the upper mountain has loose rock that demands attention. Summit views of the Elk Mountains are spectacular.

reviews.title: Classic Elk Mountains peak
reviews.body: Combined Castle and Conundrum for a great day. The northeast ridge is moderate and the scenery is outstanding. Bring gaiters for the willows.

routes.name: Castle-Conundrum Traverse
routes.description: This route combines Castle Peak with neighboring Conundrum Peak via a connecting ridgeline traverse. After summiting Castle via the northeast ridge, climbers traverse south to tag Conundrum Peak before descending. The traverse adds minimal difficulty but provides a second summit.
routes.summary: Ridge traverse connecting Castle Peak with Conundrum Peak for a two-summit day.
routes.safetyNotes: The traverse ridge has some exposure and loose rock. Budget extra time for the additional peak.

tips.content: Summit Castle first, then traverse to Conundrum for the most efficient route.
The connecting ridge is straightforward but has some loose rock sections.

gear.notes: Loose rock on the traverse ridge
Helpful for route finding on the traverse

reviews.title: Two peaks for the price of one
reviews.body: The Castle-Conundrum combo is a great way to bag two peaks in a day. The traverse is fun and adds only a little time. Both summits have excellent views.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Quandary Peak is one of the most popular 14er hikes in Colorado due to its accessibility from Breckenridge and moderate difficulty. The well-maintained trail ascends the broad east ridge above treeline with sweeping views of the Tenmile Range. An excellent choice for a first 14er.
routes.summary: Very popular and accessible standard route ideal for a first 14er attempt.
routes.safetyNotes: Extremely popular; expect crowds on summer weekends. The upper ridge is exposed to weather. Start early for parking and weather.

tips.content: This is one of the most accessible 14ers from Denver and makes an excellent first 14er.
Arrive very early on weekends as the parking lot overflows by 6 AM in summer.
The trail is entirely above treeline so bring sun protection and rain gear.

gear.notes: Entirely above treeline
Afternoon storms common
Helpful on the descent

reviews.title: Perfect first 14er
reviews.body: Did this as my first 14er and loved it. Well-maintained trail, stunning views, and a great sense of accomplishment. Just be prepared for crowds.

reviews.title: Crowded but classic
reviews.body: The trail felt like a highway on a Saturday but the views from the summit are worth it. Great warm-up peak for harder objectives.

routes.name: Cristo Couloir
routes.description: A dramatic alternative to the standard east ridge, the Cristo Couloir ascends a steep gully on the northwest face of Quandary Peak. In winter and spring, this is a popular ski and snow climb. In summer, it involves loose scree and Class 3 scrambling. The route is much steeper and more challenging than the standard route.
routes.summary: Steep northwest couloir offering a challenging alternative to the standard hiking trail.
routes.safetyNotes: The couloir holds snow into early summer. In summer, loose scree makes footing treacherous. Rockfall danger is significant with parties above. Helmet required.

tips.content: This route is best done as a snow climb in spring or early summer when the scree is consolidated.
In summer conditions, the loose scree makes this much harder than the Class 3 rating suggests.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall in the couloir
Needed if snow is present in the couloir

reviews.title: Fun snow climb in spring
reviews.body: Did this as a spring snow climb and it was outstanding. Firm snow made the ascent straightforward with ice axe and crampons. Summer scree conditions sound much worse.
reviews.conditions: Firm spring snow, clear skies, late May

routes.name: Mount Evans Road Walk
routes.description: The simplest way to summit Mount Evans on foot follows the paved Mount Evans Scenic Byway from Summit Lake to the summit parking area. While many visitors drive to the top, hiking from Summit Lake provides a rewarding walk with minimal elevation gain. The road is the highest paved road in North America.
routes.summary: Easy walk along the highest paved road in North America from Summit Lake.
routes.safetyNotes: Watch for vehicle traffic on the road. Altitude sickness is common due to the high starting elevation. Road is seasonal and typically open Memorial Day to Labor Day.

tips.content: The road is typically open Memorial Day through Labor Day; check conditions before going.
Watch for mountain goats near the summit; they are very habituated to humans.
Walk on the road shoulder and face oncoming traffic for safety.

gear.notes: Summit can be very cold and windy even in summer
For visibility walking along the road
Intense UV at 14000+ feet

reviews.title: Easiest 14er but feels odd
reviews.body: Walking along a road with cars driving past is a strange 14er experience. But the views are fantastic and the mountain goats are entertaining. A good option for those wanting an easy summit.

reviews.title: Great for beginners or off days
reviews.body: Sometimes you just want an easy summit day. The road walk from Summit Lake is pleasant and the summit area has incredible views. Bring warm layers; it was 40F on top in July.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, cold wind, late July

routes.name: Chicago Lakes Trail
routes.description: A much more rewarding and challenging approach to Mount Evans via the Chicago Lakes trail from the Echo Lake area. The trail passes through beautiful forests and past alpine lakes before climbing steep slopes to the summit ridge. This route gives a genuine mountain climbing experience compared to the road walk.
routes.summary: Rewarding trail through forests and alpine lakes for a genuine mountain experience.
routes.safetyNotes: Upper slopes are steep and can hold snow into July. The trail above Chicago Lakes becomes less defined. Watch for weather on the exposed upper mountain.

tips.content: This route provides a true mountain experience compared to the road walk from Summit Lake.
The Chicago Lakes themselves make a worthy destination even without summiting.

gear.notes: Helpful on the steep upper slopes
Trail becomes faint above the lakes

reviews.title: The real way to climb Evans
reviews.body: Forget the road walk. Chicago Lakes is the way to experience Mount Evans. Beautiful lakes, genuine mountain terrain, and a real sense of accomplishment. Much more rewarding than driving up.
reviews.conditions: Clear skies, some lingering snow patches, early July

routes.name: Navajo Lake Approach
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Wilson approaches from Navajo Lake and ascends the north slopes. This is one of the more difficult standard 14er routes in Colorado, featuring Class 4 rock climbing on the upper mountain. The approach through Navajo Basin is spectacular but the summit push requires solid scrambling skills and comfort with exposure.
routes.summary: Technical Class 4 route through stunning Navajo Basin to a challenging summit.
routes.safetyNotes: Class 4 moves near the summit require solid climbing skills. Loose rock is a constant concern. A helmet is mandatory. Consider a rope for less experienced members of your party.

tips.content: Camp at Navajo Lake or in the basin to allow an early start for the long, technical day.
The Class 4 sections are short but exposed; a rope may provide peace of mind.
Mount Wilson, Wilson Peak, and El Diente form a trio that strong parties can combine.

gear.notes: Mandatory for loose rock on the upper mountain
Optional for belaying the Class 4 sections
Recommended for overnight at Navajo Lake

reviews.title: Serious mountain with serious views
reviews.body: Mount Wilson is not to be taken lightly. The Class 4 sections near the summit require real climbing skills. But the Navajo Basin is gorgeous and the summit views are world-class.
reviews.conditions: Clear and cold, light wind, late July

reviews.title: One of Colorado's finest
reviews.body: Camped at Navajo Lake and summited early morning. The technical climbing is exciting and the mountain has a true alpine feel. One of my favorite 14ers.
reviews.conditions: Predawn start, clear skies, calm, early August

routes.name: Rock of Ages Route
routes.description: An alternate approach to Mount Wilson via the Rock of Ages saddle from Silver Pick Basin. This route approaches from the south and offers different scenery than the Navajo Lake route. The upper mountain still involves Class 4 climbing. Often used as part of a traverse with El Diente Peak.
routes.summary: Southern approach via Rock of Ages saddle with Class 4 summit climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: Similar technical difficulties to the Navajo Lake approach. The Rock of Ages traverse has exposure. Helmet mandatory.

tips.content: This approach works well if combining Mount Wilson with El Diente Peak.
The Silver Pick Basin road requires high clearance 4WD.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall protection
Good grip important for the Class 4 rock

reviews.title: Great approach for the Wilson group
reviews.body: Used this route to combine Mount Wilson and El Diente. The Rock of Ages area is beautiful and the route is logical. Technical sections are manageable for experienced scramblers.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, early morning, late July

routes.name: Lincoln/Cameron/Democrat/Bross Traverse
routes.description: Mount Cameron is almost always climbed as part of the famous Decalibron loop which traverses four 14ers from Kite Lake. Cameron sits between Lincoln and Bross on a gentle ridgeline and is the easiest of the four to summit. The loop is one of the most efficient multi-summit days in Colorado.
routes.summary: Usually climbed as part of the Decalibron loop connecting four 14ers from Kite Lake.
routes.safetyNotes: The entire loop is above treeline with no shelter. Extended time at high altitude across four summits. Watch weather carefully and be prepared to bail if storms approach.

tips.content: Cameron is just a bump on the ridge between Lincoln and Bross; tag it on the way through.
The full Decalibron loop covers Democrat, Cameron, Lincoln, and Bross.
Start with Democrat going counter-clockwise for the most efficient loop.

gear.notes: Exposed ridges throughout the traverse
Long day above 13000 feet with no water sources
Entirely above treeline for many hours

reviews.title: Four 14ers in a day
reviews.body: Cameron is just a brief stop on the Decalibron loop but it counts as a 14er. The entire traverse is a fantastic day out. Easy terrain throughout.

reviews.title: More of a ridge bump than a peak
reviews.body: Cameron barely feels like a separate summit but the Decalibron loop it is part of is excellent. Four peaks in one moderate day of hiking.

routes.name: East Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Shavano ascends the east slopes from the Blank Gulch trailhead. The trail is well-maintained and climbs steadily through forest before emerging above treeline for the final push to the summit. This is the most straightforward route and is commonly combined with neighboring Tabeguache Peak.
routes.summary: Standard east slopes route commonly combined with Tabeguache Peak.
routes.safetyNotes: The upper slopes have some loose rock. Start early to avoid afternoon storms on the exposed summit area. Consider combining with Tabeguache.

tips.content: Combine with Tabeguache Peak for a rewarding two-summit day via the connecting ridge.
The trail through the forest is well-shaded but carries no water above the first mile.
If combining with Tabeguache, summit Shavano first then traverse north.

gear.notes: Helpful on the steep descent
Afternoon storms frequent in the Sawatch
No reliable water above the first mile

reviews.title: Solid Sawatch hike
reviews.body: A straightforward route that delivers great views. Combined with Tabeguache for a very satisfying day. The trail is well-maintained and easy to follow.

reviews.title: Great Shavano-Tabeguache combo
reviews.body: Did both peaks in a day starting with Shavano. The connecting ridge is easy and adds Tabeguache without much extra effort. Start early for the long day.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, light wind, late July

routes.name: Angel of Shavano
routes.description: This route follows the Angel of Shavano drainage, a prominent snow formation visible from the valley below. The trail climbs the eastern slopes via the Angel couloir, which provides a slightly different experience from the standard east slopes. The route is named for the angel-shaped snowfield that persists into early summer.
routes.summary: Scenic alternate route following the Angel of Shavano snowfield drainage.
routes.safetyNotes: The Angel couloir can hold snow into July. Bring an ice axe if snow is present. Otherwise similar hazards to the standard route.

tips.content: The Angel snowfield is most visible and photogenic from the valley in May and June.
If snow is still present in the couloir, an ice axe and crampons may be needed.

gear.notes: Needed if snow persists in the Angel couloir
For lingering snow patches

reviews.title: Unique route with history
reviews.body: The Angel of Shavano is a cool piece of Colorado mountain lore. The route follows the drainage where the angel snowfield forms. A bit longer than the standard route but interesting.
reviews.conditions: Clear, patchy snow in couloir, late June

routes.name: West Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Belford ascends the west slopes from the Missouri Gulch trailhead. The trail is well-maintained and moderately steep, passing through forest before reaching the alpine zone. This is one of the more straightforward Sawatch Range 14ers and is frequently combined with Mount Oxford.
routes.summary: Well-maintained trail up the west slopes, frequently combined with Mount Oxford.
routes.safetyNotes: Straightforward route with standard 14er hazards. Start early to avoid afternoon storms. The Belford-Oxford saddle can be windy.

tips.content: Combine with Mount Oxford by traversing the easy connecting ridge for two 14ers.
Missouri Mountain can also be added for a challenging three-peak day.
The trail is steep but well-graded with good switchbacks.

gear.notes: Helpful on the steep descent
Exposed summit with afternoon storm potential
Above treeline for most of the route

reviews.title: Efficient two-peak day
reviews.body: Did Belford and Oxford together for a great day. The trail up Belford is steep but straightforward. The traverse to Oxford is easy and scenic.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds by noon, mid-July

reviews.title: Well-maintained trail
reviews.body: One of the better-maintained 14er trails. The grade is steady and the route is obvious. Combined with Oxford and even added Missouri for an epic day.

routes.name: Belford-Oxford Combo
routes.description: This popular route combines Mount Belford and Mount Oxford in a single outing by ascending Belford via the west slopes and then traversing the gentle ridge south to Oxford before descending back to the Missouri Gulch trailhead. The traverse adds minimal difficulty and provides a very efficient two-peak day.
routes.summary: Popular two-peak combo traversing the ridge between Belford and Oxford.
routes.safetyNotes: Extended time above treeline on the connecting ridge. Watch weather carefully as the ridge offers no shelter.

tips.content: Summit Belford first, then traverse to Oxford and descend the Belford trail for the most efficient loop.
The connecting ridge between Belford and Oxford is gentle and scenic.

gear.notes: The connecting ridge can be windy
Long day with no water above treeline

reviews.title: Best two-peak combo in the Sawatch
reviews.body: Belford and Oxford are a natural pair. The traverse is easy and the views of the Collegiate Peaks are outstanding. Highly recommend doing both in a day.

routes.name: South Face/Ellingwood Arete
routes.description: The Ellingwood Arete is one of the most famous technical climbing routes on any Colorado 14er. This classic route ascends the dramatic south face of Crestone Needle via a prominent arete with sustained 5th class climbing and incredible exposure. The rock is generally solid Conglomerate and the climbing is exhilarating. A rope and protection are recommended.
routes.summary: Famous technical climbing route on the dramatic south face arete with sustained 5th class.
routes.safetyNotes: This is a technical rock climbing route requiring rope, protection, and experience leading at the grade. The route has significant exposure and retreat is difficult once committed. Acclimatize before attempting.

tips.content: Camp at South Colony Lakes and acclimate for a day before attempting this technical route.
Bring a single rack of cams and a set of nuts for protection on the 5th class sections.
Start at first light as the route is long and you need to be off the summit before afternoon storms.

gear.notes: Essential for the technical climbing sections
Single rack needed for protection
Mandatory for rockfall and leader fall protection

reviews.title: Best alpine rock route in Colorado
reviews.body: The Ellingwood Arete is everything it's cracked up to be. Sustained, exposed, and absolutely thrilling climbing on a 14er. The summit register was a proud moment.
reviews.conditions: Clear and calm, cold start, late July

reviews.title: A must-do for alpine climbers
reviews.body: If you climb at 5.4 and enjoy exposure, this route is a bucket-list item. The position on the arete is incredible. We brought a single rack and it was sufficient.
reviews.conditions: Predawn start, clear, light wind, early August

routes.name: Crestone Needle-Peak Traverse
routes.description: This challenging traverse connects Crestone Needle to Crestone Peak along the knife-edge ridge between them. The route involves sustained Class 4 scrambling with significant exposure and some loose rock. This is one of the most difficult standard traverses in the Colorado 14ers and requires excellent scrambling skills.
routes.summary: Challenging Class 4 traverse connecting Crestone Needle and Crestone Peak.
routes.safetyNotes: This traverse has serious exposure and loose rock. Many parties use a rope for the most exposed sections. Retreat from the middle of the traverse is very difficult. Only for experienced alpine scramblers.

tips.content: Camp at South Colony Lakes for multiple days to allow acclimatization and weather flexibility.
A 30m rope is recommended for the most exposed sections of the traverse.

gear.notes: Strongly recommended for exposed traverse sections
Mandatory for the loose rock on the traverse

reviews.title: Ultimate Colorado scramble
reviews.body: The Needle-Peak traverse is the most serious scramble I've done in Colorado. The exposure is breathtaking and the route finding keeps you engaged. Not for the faint of heart.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, cold start from camp, early August

routes.name: East Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Princeton ascends the east slopes from the Mount Princeton Hot Springs area. The trail climbs steeply through forest and across open slopes to the broad summit ridge. This is the most popular route and can be combined with a post-hike soak in the hot springs.
routes.summary: Standard route with a bonus post-hike soak in nearby hot springs.
routes.safetyNotes: The upper east slopes are steep and have loose rock sections. The trail is relentlessly steep. Start early for storms.

tips.content: Reward yourself with a soak at Mount Princeton Hot Springs after the hike.
The trail is steep from the start; pace yourself for the sustained climb.
The upper slopes have loose footing; trekking poles help on the descent.

gear.notes: Very helpful on the steep, loose descent
For the hot springs after your hike
Afternoon storms common

reviews.title: Hot springs after a 14er - perfect
reviews.body: The hike is steep but the reward of soaking in hot springs afterward is unbeatable. Great views of the Arkansas Valley from the summit.

reviews.title: Steep but rewarding
reviews.body: Mount Princeton is steeper than most Sawatch peaks. The trail gains elevation quickly. But the summit views and post-hike hot springs make it worthwhile.

routes.name: Tigger Peak Traverse
routes.description: An alternate approach to Mount Princeton that traverses Tigger Peak on the way to the summit. This route adds Class 3 scrambling and a more adventurous element to the standard East Slopes hike. The traverse provides excellent views of the Chalk Cliffs.
routes.summary: More adventurous approach traversing Tigger Peak with Class 3 scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: The Tigger Peak traverse has some exposure and loose rock. Route finding skills are needed. Not recommended in wet conditions.

tips.content: The traverse provides great views of the dramatic Chalk Cliffs on Princeton's east face.
Study the route beforehand as trail markings are sparse on the traverse.

gear.notes: Recommended for loose rock on the traverse
Route finding is essential on this traverse

reviews.title: Fun scrambling alternative
reviews.body: If the standard east slopes seem too straightforward, the Tigger traverse adds excitement. Class 3 scrambling with great views. Route finding keeps you on your toes.

routes.name: Southwest Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Yale follows the southwest slopes from the Denny Creek trailhead. The trail is well-maintained and climbs through forest before traversing open alpine slopes to the summit. This is one of the more moderate Collegiate Peaks and offers excellent views of the surrounding Sawatch Range.
routes.summary: Well-maintained standard trail through forest and alpine terrain to the summit.
routes.safetyNotes: Standard 14er hazards. The upper slopes are exposed to wind and lightning. Start early.

tips.content: The Denny Creek trailhead has limited parking; arrive early on weekends.
The forest section provides welcome shade on hot days.
Enjoy views of the other Collegiate Peaks from Yale's summit.

gear.notes: Helpful on the descent
Summit area can be windy
Extended time above treeline

reviews.title: Moderate Collegiate Peak
reviews.body: Yale is a straightforward and enjoyable 14er. The trail is in great shape and the summit offers panoramic views. A good choice for building 14er experience.

reviews.title: Nice Sawatch hike
reviews.body: Well-maintained trail with a steady grade. The alpine section above treeline is beautiful. Summit views of the Collegiate Peaks are excellent.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: An alternate approach to Mount Yale via the east ridge, offering a different perspective and less crowded conditions than the standard southwest slopes. The route climbs through Avalanche Gulch before gaining the east ridge which leads to the summit. Slightly longer but more scenic.
routes.summary: Less crowded alternate route via the east ridge with scenic Avalanche Gulch approach.
routes.safetyNotes: Trail is less defined than the standard route above treeline. Carry navigation tools.

tips.content: This route offers more solitude than the popular southwest slopes.
Route finding above treeline requires attention; follow cairns where available.

gear.notes: Helpful above treeline where trail is faint
Exposed ridge with no shelter

reviews.title: Quieter than the standard route
reviews.body: Chose the east ridge for solitude and was not disappointed. The Avalanche Gulch approach is pretty and the ridge walk is enjoyable. A bit more route finding required.

routes.name: West Slopes (Decalibron Loop)
routes.description: Mount Bross is almost exclusively climbed as the final peak in the Decalibron loop from Kite Lake. The west slopes route descends gentle tundra from the Cameron-Bross saddle to the Bross summit, then continues down to Kite Lake to complete the loop. The terrain is easy and the route is obvious.
routes.summary: Final peak in the Decalibron loop with easy terrain descending back to Kite Lake.
routes.safetyNotes: Note that Bross has private land access issues. Check current access status before climbing. The entire Decalibron is above treeline.

tips.content: Check current access status as Bross has had periodic private land closures.
Bross is typically the last peak in the Decalibron loop going counter-clockwise.
The descent from Bross back to Kite Lake is gentle and makes a nice finish to the loop.

gear.notes: Exposed ridgeline throughout
No water sources on the loop
Entirely above treeline

reviews.title: Nice finish to the Decalibron
reviews.body: Bross is an easy final summit on the loop. The descent back to Kite Lake is gentle and pleasant. Check land access before going.

reviews.title: Easy peak with access concerns
reviews.body: The peak itself is unremarkable but as part of the Decalibron it works perfectly. Make sure land access is open before planning your trip.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, moderate wind, late July

routes.name: Challenger Point Traverse
routes.description: The most popular route on Kit Carson Mountain first summits Challenger Point and then traverses the connecting ridge to Kit Carson. The traverse involves Class 3 scrambling with some exposure. The approach from the Willow Creek trailhead is long but the double summit day is very rewarding.
routes.summary: Popular route traversing from Challenger Point with Class 3 ridge scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: The traverse between Challenger and Kit Carson has sustained exposure and loose rock. Helmet recommended. The long approach means a very long day unless you backpack in.

tips.content: Consider backpacking to the upper basin and camping to split this into two shorter days.
Summit Challenger first, then traverse to Kit Carson for the most logical flow.
The Class 3 sections on the traverse require careful hand and foot placement.

gear.notes: Loose rock on the traverse ridge
For overnight in the upper basin
Helpful for route finding on the traverse

reviews.title: Two amazing peaks in one day
reviews.body: Backpacked to the upper basin and did both peaks the next morning. The traverse between them is exciting Class 3 with great exposure. Sangre de Cristo views are incredible.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cool, early start from camp, late July

reviews.title: Long but rewarding combo
reviews.body: The Challenger-Kit Carson combo is a fantastic objective. The traverse keeps you engaged and both summits offer stunning views. Backpacking in is strongly recommended.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds by noon, early August

routes.name: Kit Carson Avenue
routes.description: Kit Carson Avenue is a ledge system on the south face of Kit Carson Mountain that provides a more direct but more technical route to the summit. The route follows a series of ledges with Class 4 moves and significant exposure. This is a serious route that requires climbing experience and comfort with exposure.
routes.summary: Technical Class 4 ledge system on the south face with significant exposure.
routes.safetyNotes: This is a serious Class 4 route with significant exposure. Route finding is critical as wrong turns lead to dead ends on cliff faces. Not recommended for those uncomfortable with exposure.

tips.content: Study the route carefully before attempting; wrong turns on the ledge system can be dangerous.
The Avenue is best done in dry conditions when the rock offers good friction.

gear.notes: Mandatory for rockfall protection
Optional for belaying the most exposed sections

reviews.title: Exciting route for experienced scramblers
reviews.body: Kit Carson Avenue is a unique route on a ledge system with real exposure. Route finding is the crux. One wrong turn and you're in serious terrain. Very rewarding when done correctly.
reviews.conditions: Dry, clear, calm morning, late July

routes.name: North Face
routes.description: The standard route on El Diente Peak ascends the north face from Navajo Basin. This is a demanding route with sustained Class 3 scrambling on loose rock. El Diente is one of the more remote and challenging 14ers in Colorado, requiring solid scrambling skills and good fitness.
routes.summary: Demanding Class 3 route up the north face from remote Navajo Basin.
routes.safetyNotes: The rock on El Diente is notoriously loose. Helmet is mandatory. The peak is remote and evacuation would be slow. Climb with a partner.

tips.content: Camp at Navajo Lake to allow an early start for this demanding objective.
The rock quality is poor; test every handhold before committing your weight.
Consider combining with Mount Wilson via the challenging connecting traverse.

gear.notes: Mandatory for the extremely loose rock
Protects hands during sustained scrambling
Remote location with slow evacuation

reviews.title: Loose but rewarding
reviews.body: El Diente has some of the worst rock quality of any 14er. But the remote setting in Navajo Basin is beautiful and the summit views are outstanding. Be extremely careful with the rock.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cool, early morning start from camp, late July

reviews.title: Serious mountain in a serious range
reviews.body: The Wilson Group is no joke. El Diente's loose rock demands constant attention. Rewarding summit for those who earn it.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, predawn start, early August

routes.name: Traverse from Mount Wilson
routes.description: The famous traverse between Mount Wilson and El Diente Peak is one of the most difficult standard routes connecting two 14ers. The traverse involves sustained Class 4 scrambling on notoriously loose rock with extreme exposure. This is a serious undertaking reserved for experienced alpine climbers.
routes.summary: Famous and difficult Class 4 traverse connecting Mount Wilson to El Diente Peak.
routes.safetyNotes: This is one of the most serious standard routes on any Colorado 14er. The rock is extremely loose and the exposure is severe. A rope is recommended. Only for experienced alpine climbers.

tips.content: A 30m rope and a light rack are strongly recommended for the most exposed sections.
Most parties traverse from Wilson to El Diente as the route finding is more intuitive in that direction.

gear.notes: Strongly recommended for the exposed traverse
Absolutely mandatory for the loose rock

reviews.title: Most intense scramble in Colorado
reviews.body: The Wilson-El Diente traverse is no joke. Sustained Class 4 on terrible rock with massive exposure. We roped up for several sections. Incredibly rewarding but not for the inexperienced.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, predawn alpine start from Navajo Lake camp, early August

routes.name: Southwest Ridge (Shavano Combo)
routes.description: Tabeguache Peak is almost always climbed in combination with Mount Shavano via the connecting ridge. After summiting Shavano, climbers traverse the gentle ridge north to Tabeguache and then descend via the southwest ridge. The terrain is moderate and the route adds a rewarding second summit to the Shavano outing.
routes.summary: Usually combined with Shavano via a gentle ridge traverse for a two-peak day.
routes.safetyNotes: Extended time above treeline on the connecting ridge. Watch weather carefully. The descent trail from Tabeguache can be faint.

tips.content: Summit Shavano first, then traverse to Tabeguache for the most efficient combo.
The connecting ridge between Shavano and Tabeguache is gentle and scenic.
The descent from Tabeguache back to the Shavano trail can be faint; use GPS if needed.

gear.notes: Helpful for the descent trail which can be faint
Long day with no water above treeline
Ridge can be windy

reviews.title: Natural combo with Shavano
reviews.body: Tabeguache is a great bonus peak when doing Shavano. The traverse is easy and adds maybe 90 minutes. Both summits have excellent views.

reviews.title: Two for one
reviews.body: The Shavano-Tabeguache combo is one of the best two-peak days in the Sawatch. Easy terrain throughout and the ridge walk between them is enjoyable.

routes.name: West Slopes (Belford Combo)
routes.description: Mount Oxford is most commonly climbed in combination with Mount Belford via the connecting ridge. After summiting Belford, climbers descend to the saddle and climb the gentle ridge to Oxford's summit. The terrain is moderate and the route is straightforward.
routes.summary: Most commonly climbed via gentle ridge traverse from Mount Belford.
routes.safetyNotes: The connecting ridge is exposed to weather and wind. Extended time above treeline. Watch for storms.

tips.content: Climb Belford first, traverse to Oxford, then return to descend via the Belford trail.
The Belford-Oxford saddle is a good place to reassess weather before continuing.
Strong parties can add Missouri Mountain for a three-peak day.

gear.notes: Ridge between Belford and Oxford is often windy
Helpful on the descent
Long day if combining with Belford

reviews.title: Great add-on to Belford
reviews.body: Oxford makes a perfect companion to Belford. The traverse is easy and scenic and adds a second summit with minimal extra effort.

routes.name: South Ridge
routes.description: An alternate route that ascends Oxford directly via the south ridge without going over Belford first. This route is less commonly used but offers a more direct approach to Oxford. The trail follows Pine Creek before climbing the south ridge to the summit.
routes.summary: Direct approach to Oxford via the south ridge, bypassing Belford.
routes.safetyNotes: Less traveled route with fainter trail. Carry navigation tools.

tips.content: This route is a good option if you only want to climb Oxford without Belford.
The trail is less defined than the Belford approach; bring a GPS.

gear.notes: Trail is faint on the upper ridge
Exposed ridge with no shelter

reviews.title: Quiet but less scenic than the Belford approach
reviews.body: Used this route to climb Oxford independently. It works but honestly the Belford combo is more enjoyable and gives you two peaks. Trail is faint above treeline.

routes.name: South Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Sneffels ascends the south slopes from Yankee Boy Basin via the prominent V-Notch couloir. The approach through Yankee Boy Basin is stunningly beautiful with wildflowers in July. The upper route involves Class 3 scrambling through the couloir and up the final summit block.
routes.summary: Classic route through scenic Yankee Boy Basin with Class 3 couloir scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: The V-Notch couloir has rockfall danger, especially with parties above. Helmet is essential. The couloir holds snow into early summer requiring an ice axe.

tips.content: Visit in mid-July for the incredible wildflower display in Yankee Boy Basin.
The Yankee Boy Basin road requires high clearance 4WD for the upper section.
Start early to minimize rockfall risk in the couloir from other parties.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall in the couloir
Needed if snow persists in the couloir
Helpful for the Class 3 scrambling

reviews.title: Most scenic 14er approach in Colorado
reviews.body: Yankee Boy Basin in wildflower season is jaw-dropping. The climb through the V-Notch is exciting and the summit views of the San Juans are incredible. A must-do 14er.

reviews.title: Classic San Juan peak
reviews.body: Sneffels is everything a 14er should be. Beautiful approach, exciting scrambling, and a stunning summit. The couloir requires a helmet and an early start.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, light wind, late July

routes.name: Snake Couloir
routes.description: The Snake Couloir is a dramatic alternative to the standard south slopes route, ascending a narrow couloir on the north side of Mount Sneffels. This is a more technical and committing route with Class 4 climbing and significant exposure. Popular as a spring snow climb when the couloir is filled.
routes.summary: Technical Class 4 couloir on the north face, popular as a spring snow climb.
routes.safetyNotes: In spring, avalanche assessment is critical. In summer, the couloir is loose rock and scree. Best done as a snow climb in stable spring conditions. Only for experienced mountaineers.

tips.content: Best done as a spring snow climb when the couloir is consolidated and filled.
Avalanche assessment skills and equipment are essential for the spring ascent.

gear.notes: Essential for the steep snow climb
Required for firm spring snow

reviews.title: Incredible spring snow climb
reviews.body: The Snake Couloir in spring is one of the best snow climbs in Colorado. Firm neve, dramatic exposure, and a thrilling summit finish. Avalanche skills are a must.
reviews.conditions: Firm spring snow, clear, cold, late April

routes.name: East Ridge (Decalibron)
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Democrat ascends the east ridge from Kite Lake as part of the Decalibron loop. Democrat is typically the first summit in the counter-clockwise loop. The trail is well-defined and the grade is moderate, making this an excellent beginner 14er.
routes.summary: First peak in the popular Decalibron loop with a well-defined trail from Kite Lake.
routes.safetyNotes: Entirely above treeline with no shelter. Start early if doing the full Decalibron to allow time for all four peaks.

tips.content: Start with Democrat when doing the Decalibron loop counter-clockwise.
Kite Lake parking fills fast; arrive before 5:30 AM on summer weekends.
The east ridge has a well-worn trail that is easy to follow.

gear.notes: Ridge is exposed and often windy
Above treeline the entire route
Kite Lake is cold in early morning

reviews.title: Great start to the Decalibron
reviews.body: Democrat is a perfect warm-up for the Decalibron loop. Easy trail, quick summit, and then you're off to Cameron and Lincoln. Four 14ers in one day is hard to beat.

reviews.title: Easy and accessible
reviews.body: One of the easiest 14ers in Colorado. The trail from Kite Lake is short and well-defined. Great for beginners or as a quick summit.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, moderate wind, late July

routes.name: Kite Lake Approach
routes.description: A direct approach to Mount Democrat from Kite Lake without doing the full Decalibron loop. This variation ascends the northwest face more directly and involves some Class 2 talus scrambling. Shorter and more direct than the standard east ridge for those only wanting Democrat.
routes.summary: Direct approach from Kite Lake for those only wanting to summit Democrat.
routes.safetyNotes: The direct face route has some loose talus. Stay on the trail to minimize erosion.

tips.content: This is a good option if you only want Democrat and not the full Decalibron.
The talus on the direct route is loose; watch your footing.

gear.notes: Ankle support for the talus sections
Helpful for stability on loose rock

reviews.title: Quick summit
reviews.body: Used the direct route for a quick summit on a day with questionable weather. Short and efficient. The talus is a bit tedious but it gets you to the top fast.

routes.name: S Ridge/Snowmass Creek
routes.description: The standard route on Snowmass Mountain approaches from Snowmass Creek via a very long trail before ascending the south ridge. This is one of the most remote 14ers in Colorado and the approach is among the longest. The upper ridge involves Class 3 scrambling on sometimes loose rock. Most parties backpack to Snowmass Lake.
routes.summary: Long approach via Snowmass Creek with Class 3 scrambling on the south ridge.
routes.safetyNotes: Extremely long approach; plan for a multi-day trip. The south ridge has loose rock and some exposure. Remote location means slow evacuation. Permits may be required for camping.

tips.content: This is typically a multi-day backpacking trip with camp at Snowmass Lake.
Check permit requirements for camping in the Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness.
Snowmass Lake is one of the most beautiful alpine lakes in Colorado.

gear.notes: Multi-day trip is essentially required
Loose rock on the south ridge
Required in Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness

reviews.title: Remote wilderness gem
reviews.body: Snowmass Mountain is the ultimate Colorado 14er experience. The long approach rewards you with stunning Snowmass Lake and a challenging summit. A true wilderness adventure.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cool, backpacked in over two days, early August

reviews.title: Earn every step
reviews.body: The approach is brutally long but the setting is unmatched. Snowmass Lake alone is worth the hike. The summit scramble is engaging and the views are world-class.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, late July

routes.name: West Face
routes.description: The west face of Snowmass Mountain offers a more technical and direct route to the summit from the Geneva Lake area. This route involves Class 4 climbing on steep terrain and is less traveled than the standard south ridge. The approach from Lead King Basin provides a different perspective of the mountain.
routes.summary: Technical west face route from Geneva Lake with Class 4 climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: Technical route requiring climbing experience. Remote location. A rope may be needed for the most difficult sections.

tips.content: This approach from Geneva Lake sees very few climbers.
Bring a rope and basic protection for the Class 4 sections.

gear.notes: Recommended for the Class 4 sections
Mandatory for loose rock

reviews.title: Adventurous alternative
reviews.body: The west face sees almost nobody. The climbing is engaging and the Geneva Lake basin is beautiful. Bring a rope for peace of mind on the upper face.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, early start from Geneva Lake camp, early August

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Eolus ascends the northeast ridge from the Chicago Basin approach. Access to Chicago Basin typically involves riding the Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad to the Needleton trailhead, followed by a long hike to camp. The upper ridge involves fun Class 3 scrambling on relatively solid rock.
routes.summary: Classic route via train-accessed Chicago Basin with fun Class 3 ridge scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: Remote location accessed by train. Plan for multi-day trip. The upper ridge has some exposure. Lightning is a serious concern in the Needles area.

tips.content: Book your Durango & Silverton train tickets well in advance; they sell out quickly.
Plan for at least 3 days: day 1 hike in, day 2 summit, day 3 hike out.
Consider combining with Windom and Sunlight peaks from the same base camp.

gear.notes: Multi-day trip required
For the Class 3 scrambling on the ridge
Required in the Weminuche Wilderness

reviews.title: Train ride plus 14ers equals magic
reviews.body: The train ride to the trailhead is an experience in itself. Chicago Basin is spectacular and the climb up Eolus is exciting. Combined with Windom and Sunlight for an incredible trip.
reviews.conditions: Clear mornings, afternoon storms, early August

reviews.title: Best 14er adventure in Colorado
reviews.body: The Needles trio from Chicago Basin is the ultimate Colorado mountaineering objective. Eolus is the most straightforward of the three. The setting is unparalleled.
reviews.conditions: Mixed weather, clear summit morning, late July

routes.name: Catwalk Approach
routes.description: This variation approaches Mount Eolus via the Catwalk, a narrow ledge system that connects to the upper northeast ridge. The Catwalk adds a dramatic element to the climb with some exposure. The approach is the same via Chicago Basin but the upper route takes a slightly different line.
routes.summary: Variation using the dramatic Catwalk ledge system to reach the upper ridge.
routes.safetyNotes: The Catwalk has significant exposure on a narrow ledge. Not for those uncomfortable with heights. The rest of the route is similar to the standard NE ridge.

tips.content: The Catwalk is a narrow ledge with serious exposure; only attempt if comfortable with heights.
The Catwalk connects naturally to the upper NE ridge route.

gear.notes: Essential for the upper mountain scrambling
Helpful for the sustained scrambling

reviews.title: The Catwalk adds excitement
reviews.body: The Catwalk is a fun addition to the standard route. The exposure is real but the ledge is wide enough to feel secure. The scrambling above is engaging.
reviews.conditions: Clear and cool, early morning from Chicago Basin camp, late July

routes.name: West Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Windom Peak ascends the west ridge from Chicago Basin. Like the other Needles peaks, access is via the Durango & Silverton train. The route is the least technical of the three Chicago Basin 14ers and involves moderate Class 2 scrambling to the summit.
routes.summary: Least technical of the Chicago Basin 14ers with moderate Class 2 scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: Remote location requiring multi-day trip. Standard 14er hazards plus the remoteness factor. Lightning is especially dangerous in the Needles.

tips.content: Windom is often combined with Eolus and Sunlight from a Chicago Basin base camp.
The west ridge is the easiest of the three Chicago Basin 14er routes.
Start early as afternoon lightning storms are extremely common in the Needles.

gear.notes: Multi-day trip required
Recommended for loose rock sections
Afternoon storms are almost guaranteed

reviews.title: Incredible setting
reviews.body: Windom has the easiest route of the three Chicago Basin peaks but the setting is just as spectacular. The train approach and alpine meadows make this a world-class experience.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, early August

reviews.title: Most accessible Needles 14er
reviews.body: If you can only do one Chicago Basin peak, Windom is the most accessible. But honestly, do all three if you've made the effort to get in there.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, occasional light rain, late July

routes.name: Sunlight-Windom Traverse
routes.description: This route connects Sunlight Peak to Windom Peak via the dramatic ridge traverse between them. The traverse involves Class 4 scrambling with significant exposure and some loose rock. This is a serious undertaking best done as part of a multi-peak day in Chicago Basin.
routes.summary: Dramatic Class 4 ridge traverse connecting Sunlight Peak to Windom Peak.
routes.safetyNotes: The traverse has serious exposure and loose rock. A rope may be prudent for the most exposed sections. Very long day combining two technical summits.

tips.content: Most parties traverse from Sunlight to Windom as the route finding is cleaner.
Budget a full day for this traverse and start well before dawn.

gear.notes: Mandatory for the loose rock traverse
Recommended for the most exposed sections

reviews.title: Epic traverse in incredible terrain
reviews.body: The Sunlight-Windom traverse is one of the best ridge traverses in Colorado. Sustained Class 4 with great exposure and beautiful rock. A serious but rewarding day.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cool, predawn start from Chicago Basin, early August

routes.name: North Slopes from Willow Creek
routes.description: The standard route on Challenger Point ascends the north slopes from the Willow Creek trailhead. The trail passes through forest and open meadows before climbing moderate slopes to the summit. Challenger is most frequently combined with Kit Carson Mountain via the connecting ridge traverse.
routes.summary: Standard hiking route from Willow Creek, often combined with Kit Carson Mountain.
routes.safetyNotes: Long approach makes this a full day. Consider backpacking to the upper basin. The summit area is exposed to lightning.

tips.content: Consider camping in the upper basin to break the long day and allow a Kit Carson combo.
Challenger is named in honor of the Space Shuttle Challenger crew.
The trail through Willow Creek meadows is beautiful in wildflower season.

gear.notes: Helpful for the long approach and descent
Exposed summit area
For overnight in upper basin

reviews.title: Beautiful approach to a meaningful summit
reviews.body: The hike through Willow Creek is gorgeous, especially in wildflower season. The summit has a memorial plaque for the Challenger astronauts. Combined with Kit Carson for an incredible day.

reviews.title: Long but rewarding
reviews.body: The approach is long but scenic. Camped in the upper basin which made the summit day reasonable. Natural combo with Kit Carson.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, late July

routes.name: West Slopes from Harvard Combo
routes.description: Mount Columbia is most commonly climbed in combination with Mount Harvard from the Harvard route. After summiting Harvard, climbers traverse the connecting ridge south to Columbia. The terrain is moderate Class 2 throughout but the total distance for the combo is significant. Columbia can also be approached independently from the west.
routes.summary: Most commonly climbed as part of a Harvard-Columbia combo via the connecting ridge.
routes.safetyNotes: The Harvard-Columbia combo is a very long day. Extended time above treeline. The connecting ridge can be tricky to navigate. Be prepared to bail on Columbia if weather deteriorates.

tips.content: Most parties summit Harvard first, then traverse to Columbia before descending.
The connecting ridge has some route-finding challenges; bring a GPS.
Budget extra food and water for this very long day.

gear.notes: Route finding on the connecting ridge
Very long day above treeline
Helpful for the long distance and descent

reviews.title: Epic combo day
reviews.body: The Harvard-Columbia combo is a big day but incredibly rewarding. Two of the highest peaks in Colorado in a single push. The ridge between them is scenic but long.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, predawn start, late July

reviews.title: Long but worth it for two peaks
reviews.body: This is a brutally long day. Started at 3 AM and finished at 5 PM. But getting Harvard and Columbia in one shot is efficient. Bring lots of food and water.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds by noon, early August

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Missouri Mountain ascends the northwest ridge from Missouri Gulch via the same trailhead used for Belford and Oxford. Missouri is a steeper and more demanding climb than its neighbors and is sometimes added to the Belford-Oxford combo for an ambitious three-peak day.
routes.summary: Steep standard route from Missouri Gulch, sometimes combined with Belford and Oxford.
routes.safetyNotes: Missouri is steeper and more demanding than Belford or Oxford. The upper northwest ridge has some loose rock. Do not underestimate this peak.

tips.content: Missouri is the most challenging of the Belford-Oxford-Missouri trio.
If combining with Belford and Oxford, save Missouri for last as it requires the most energy.
The upper ridge is steep and loose; trekking poles help significantly on the descent.

gear.notes: Very helpful on the steep, loose descent
Recommended for the loose upper ridge
Demanding climb especially if combined with other peaks

reviews.title: The tough one in the trio
reviews.body: Missouri is noticeably harder than Belford or Oxford. The northwest ridge is steep and the footing is loose. But the summit views are excellent. Saved it for the third peak and was exhausted but happy.

reviews.title: Don't underestimate Missouri
reviews.body: Added Missouri to a Belford-Oxford day and it nearly broke me. The peak is beautiful but demands respect. The upper ridge is steep and loose.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, clouds building, early August

routes.name: West Ridge from Colony Lakes
routes.description: The standard route on Humboldt Peak ascends the west ridge from the South Colony Lakes trailhead. The trail climbs through forest and past the lakes before ascending moderate slopes to the ridge and summit. Humboldt is the easiest of the Crestone group peaks and offers spectacular views of the Crestones.
routes.summary: Easiest of the Crestone group peaks with stunning views of Crestone Peak and Needle.
routes.safetyNotes: The South Colony Lakes road is very rough and requires high clearance 4WD. Most hikers walk the road, adding distance. Start early for afternoon storms.

tips.content: The views of Crestone Peak and Crestone Needle from Humboldt's summit are some of the best in Colorado.
The South Colony road is rough; plan to walk it unless you have a very capable vehicle.
Camping at South Colony Lakes makes this a more relaxed day.

gear.notes: Helpful on the long approach and descent
Afternoon storms common
Summit views of the Crestones are world-class

reviews.title: Best views in the Sangre de Cristos
reviews.body: Humboldt itself is a straightforward hike but the views of Crestone Peak and Needle from the summit are absolutely stunning. Worth the effort just for the scenery.

reviews.title: Easiest Crestone group peak
reviews.body: If the Crestones are too technical for you, Humboldt gives you incredible views of them from a Class 2 route. The access road is brutal though.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, early August

routes.name: West Slopes
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Bierstadt from Guanella Pass is one of the most popular and accessible 14er hikes in Colorado. The trail descends briefly through willows before climbing moderate slopes to the broad summit. The short distance and moderate elevation gain make this an excellent first 14er.
routes.summary: One of the most popular and accessible 14er hikes, ideal for beginners.
routes.safetyNotes: Very popular trail; expect crowds on summer weekends. The willows at the start can be wet and muddy. Start early for parking.

tips.content: This is one of the best first 14ers due to moderate distance and the paved Guanella Pass road.
The willow bog at the start of the trail can soak your feet; gaiters help.
