Guanella Pass parking fills very fast on weekends; consider a weekday ascent.

gear.notes: Helpful for the willow bog crossing
Afternoon storms common
Mostly above treeline

reviews.title: Perfect beginner 14er
reviews.body: Did this as my first 14er and it was ideal. Short enough to not be overwhelming but still feels like an accomplishment. The willow section was muddy but manageable.

reviews.title: Crowded but classic
reviews.body: Bierstadt is deservedly popular. Easy access, moderate trail, and great views. Just be prepared for crowds and get there early for parking.

routes.name: Sawtooth Ridge
routes.description: The Sawtooth Ridge connects Mount Bierstadt to Mount Evans via a dramatic knife-edge ridge. This is one of the most famous scrambles in Colorado, featuring sustained Class 3 scrambling with significant exposure on a narrow ridge. The route is typically done from Bierstadt to Evans or as a return route after summiting Bierstadt.
routes.summary: Famous knife-edge Class 3 ridge connecting Bierstadt to Mount Evans.
routes.safetyNotes: The Sawtooth has significant exposure on a narrow ridge with some loose rock. Retreat from the middle of the ridge is difficult. Do not attempt if storms are anywhere near. Helmet required.

tips.content: Most parties go from Bierstadt toward Evans, which many consider the easier direction.
The exposure on the Sawtooth is serious; only attempt if comfortable with Class 3 exposure.
Start very early as the ridge is fully exposed to lightning with no escape.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall on the ridge
Helpful for sustained hand-over-hand scrambling
Route finding can be tricky on the ridge

reviews.title: Colorado's best scramble
reviews.body: The Sawtooth is an incredible experience. The exposure is breathtaking, the rock is generally solid, and the position on the ridge is thrilling. A must-do for scramblers.

reviews.title: Serious but exhilarating
reviews.body: Do not underestimate the Sawtooth. The exposure is real and retreat is difficult once committed. But for experienced scramblers, this is pure joy.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, early start, late July

routes.name: South Face/Red Couloir
routes.description: The standard route on Sunlight Peak ascends the south face via a couloir system from Chicago Basin. Sunlight is the most technical of the three Chicago Basin 14ers, with Class 4 climbing required on the final summit block. The summit itself is a small pointed rock requiring a committing final move.
routes.summary: Most technical Chicago Basin 14er with Class 4 summit block climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: The summit block requires a committing Class 4 move with extreme exposure. The summit is one of the smallest and most exposed in Colorado. Not for those with fear of heights.

tips.content: The final move to the summit block is the crux; study photos beforehand to understand the sequence.
Combine with Windom and Eolus from a Chicago Basin base camp for the full Needles experience.
Book your train tickets for the Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge well in advance.

gear.notes: Essential for the upper mountain scrambling
Multi-day trip via Chicago Basin
Optional for the Class 4 summit block

reviews.title: Most exciting 14er summit in Colorado
reviews.body: The final move onto Sunlight's summit block is unforgettable. Your heart pounds as you commit to the exposed Class 4 move. The smallest summit of any 14er. Incredible.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, early morning from camp, late July

reviews.title: Thrilling summit with a committing move
reviews.body: Sunlight's summit block is the most dramatic finish of any Colorado 14er. The Class 4 move is short but exposed. Beautiful peak in an incredible setting.

routes.name: Sunlight Spire
routes.description: Sunlight Spire is a prominent rock tower adjacent to Sunlight Peak's summit. The route ascends the spire via 5th class climbing with a short but thrilling pitch. This is typically done as an add-on after summiting Sunlight Peak. The spire offers a unique perspective of the Needles range.
routes.summary: Technical rock tower adjacent to Sunlight Peak requiring 5th class climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: The spire requires 5th class climbing with a rope and protection. Only for experienced rock climbers comfortable at altitude.

tips.content: Bring a short rope and a few pieces of protection to safely climb the spire.
The spire is typically done after summiting Sunlight Peak.

gear.notes: Required for the technical pitch on the spire
A few cams and nuts for protection

reviews.title: Unique summit experience
reviews.body: After doing Sunlight Peak, we couldn't resist the spire. A short pitch of fun 5.4 climbing with an incredible summit. One of the most unique objectives in Colorado.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, after Sunlight summit, late July

routes.name: West Slopes from American Basin
routes.description: The most popular route on Handies Peak starts at American Basin and follows a well-maintained trail to the summit via the west slopes. American Basin is famous for its incredible wildflower displays in July. The route is short and relatively easy, making it one of the most accessible San Juan 14ers.
routes.summary: Short, easy route from wildflower-rich American Basin to a stunning San Juan summit.
routes.safetyNotes: Easy route with standard 14er hazards. The access road to American Basin requires high clearance. Start early for afternoon storms.

tips.content: Visit in mid-July for the spectacular wildflower display in American Basin.
The access road requires high clearance; most passenger cars cannot make it.
This is one of the easier San Juan 14ers and great for a quick summit day.

gear.notes: San Juan afternoon storms can be intense
Wildflowers and summit views are outstanding
Above treeline for the entire route

reviews.title: Wildflower paradise
reviews.body: American Basin in July is one of the most beautiful places in Colorado. The wildflowers are incredible and the hike to Handies is short and easy. A perfect San Juan day.

reviews.title: Easy San Juan gem
reviews.body: Handies from American Basin is a wonderful short hike. The views from the summit span the entire San Juan range. One of my favorite easy 14ers.

routes.name: Grizzly Gulch
routes.description: An alternate approach to Handies Peak from the Grizzly Gulch trailhead near Lake City. This route is longer than the American Basin approach but starts from a more accessible trailhead. The trail follows Grizzly Gulch before climbing to the upper slopes and summit.
routes.summary: Longer alternate approach from a more accessible trailhead near Lake City.
routes.safetyNotes: Longer than the American Basin approach but with fewer road access challenges. Standard 14er hazards apply.

tips.content: This trailhead is more accessible than American Basin for lower-clearance vehicles.
The Grizzly Gulch approach can be combined with a trip to the Cinnamon Pass area.

gear.notes: Helpful for the longer distance
Afternoon storms common in the San Juans

reviews.title: Good alternative approach
reviews.body: Used Grizzly Gulch because my car couldn't make the American Basin road. Longer but still a pleasant hike with good views. The gulch is scenic in its own right.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge (Private Land Access)
routes.description: Culebra Peak is unique among Colorado 14ers as the only one on private land requiring a paid access fee. The standard route follows the northwest ridge from the Cielo Vista Ranch. The terrain is moderate Class 2 hiking across open tundra and gentle slopes. Access is limited and must be arranged in advance with the ranch.
routes.summary: Only privately-owned Colorado 14er requiring paid access and advance reservation.
routes.safetyNotes: Access must be arranged in advance with Cielo Vista Ranch and a fee is required. Limited number of climbers allowed per day. The ranch provides route information upon payment.

tips.content: You must contact Cielo Vista Ranch in advance to arrange access and pay the fee.
Limited spots are available each day; book well in advance for summer weekends.
The route is straightforward once you have ranch directions; enjoy the solitude.

gear.notes: Exposed terrain above treeline
Required fee to access the private ranch
Helpful on the moderate terrain

reviews.title: Unique 14er experience
reviews.body: Culebra is unlike any other 14er. The private access means very few people and a wilderness feel. The route is easy but the logistics of arranging access add complexity.

reviews.title: Pay to play but worth it for completionists
reviews.body: If you're going for all 58 14ers, Culebra is a must. The hiking is easy but the access fee and limited availability make it a challenge to schedule. Nice views of the Sangre de Cristos.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, moderate wind, late July

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on North Maroon Peak ascends the northeast ridge from the Maroon Lake area. This is one of the most dangerous standard 14er routes in Colorado due to the notoriously rotten Maroon Formation rock. The route involves sustained Class 4 climbing on extremely loose rock that requires constant vigilance.
routes.summary: Dangerous standard route on notoriously loose Maroon Formation rock.
routes.safetyNotes: North Maroon Peak has some of the worst rock quality of any Colorado 14er. The Maroon Bells are sometimes called the Deadly Bells for good reason. Rockfall is a constant and serious danger. Helmet is absolutely mandatory. Climb only in small parties.

tips.content: The Maroon Bells are nicknamed the Deadly Bells; take this route extremely seriously.
Climb in a very small party to minimize rockfall danger from other climbers.
Study the route thoroughly before attempting; wrong turns lead to dangerous terrain.

gear.notes: Absolutely mandatory for the terrible rock quality
Route finding is critical on loose terrain
Rock injuries are common on this route

reviews.title: Dangerous but attainable with care
reviews.body: North Maroon deserves its reputation. The rock is atrocious. Every handhold must be tested. I've done harder routes that felt much safer. Rewarding summit for those who take it seriously.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, predawn start, late July

reviews.title: Serious mountain for serious climbers
reviews.body: North Maroon is not a peak to take lightly. The rock quality demands absolute concentration. But the summit views of the Elk Range are among the best anywhere.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cold morning start, early August

routes.name: Maroon Peak-North Maroon Traverse
routes.description: The infamous traverse between Maroon Peak and North Maroon Peak is one of the most dangerous standard routes in Colorado. The traverse follows the connecting ridge on extremely loose Maroon Formation rock with severe exposure. Multiple fatalities have occurred on this route. Only for very experienced alpine climbers.
routes.summary: Infamous and dangerous ridge traverse on extremely loose rock between the Maroon Bells.
routes.safetyNotes: This is one of the most dangerous standard routes on any Colorado 14er. Multiple fatalities have occurred. The rock is among the worst in Colorado. A rope is recommended but offers limited protection on the loose terrain. Only for very experienced alpine climbers.

tips.content: This traverse has claimed multiple lives; do not attempt without extensive Class 4 experience.
A rope provides limited protection on this loose rock; experience and judgment are your best tools.

gear.notes: Absolutely mandatory; the rock is extremely loose
Offers limited protection but recommended for the most exposed sections

reviews.title: The most serious route I have ever done
reviews.body: The Maroon traverse is in a class by itself for danger. The rock is beyond terrible. Every move is calculated. I would not repeat it but I'm glad I did it once. Only for the very experienced.
reviews.conditions: Perfect weather, dry rock, predawn start, early August

routes.name: North Couloir
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Lindsey ascends the north couloir from the Lily Lake approach. The trail passes beautiful Lily Lake before climbing to the base of the couloir, which involves Class 3 scrambling on generally decent rock. The couloir provides a direct and exciting route to the summit.
routes.summary: Standard route through a north-facing couloir with Class 3 scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: The couloir has rockfall danger, especially with parties above. Helmet is essential. Snow can linger in the couloir into early July.

tips.content: The couloir holds snow into early summer; check conditions before going.
Start early to be first in the couloir and minimize rockfall from other parties.
Lily Lake at the base makes a beautiful rest stop on the approach.

gear.notes: Essential for rockfall protection in the couloir
Needed if snow persists in the couloir
Helpful for the Class 3 scrambling

reviews.title: Underrated Sangre de Cristo gem
reviews.body: Lindsey doesn't get the attention it deserves. The north couloir is fun Class 3 with solid rock. The summit views of the Sangre de Cristos and Blanca Peak are outstanding.

reviews.title: Fun scramble with great views
reviews.body: The north couloir is an enjoyable scramble. Rock quality is better than many Colorado 14er routes. Lily Lake on the approach is a nice bonus.

routes.name: Northwest Ridge
routes.description: An alternate route on Mount Lindsey that avoids the couloir by ascending the northwest ridge. This route is less technical than the north couloir but involves more route finding on moderate Class 2 terrain. A good option for those wanting to avoid the scrambling.
routes.summary: Less technical alternate route via the northwest ridge avoiding the couloir.
routes.safetyNotes: Less technical than the couloir route but requires more route finding. Trail is faint above treeline.

tips.content: This route avoids the Class 3 scrambling of the north couloir for those who prefer hiking.
Route finding above treeline requires GPS or careful map reading.

gear.notes: Trail is faint on the upper ridge
Exposed ridge with no shelter

reviews.title: Hiking alternative to the couloir
reviews.body: Chose the NW ridge to avoid the scrambling and it was a fine hike. Not as exciting as the couloir but a good option for hikers. Route finding above treeline takes attention.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge
routes.description: The southwest ridge is the standard route on Little Bear Peak, one of Colorado's most difficult and dangerous 14ers. The route ascends from Lake Como via a long approach and involves sustained Class 4 climbing with considerable exposure. The rock quality varies from decent to poor and route finding is challenging.
routes.summary: Standard route on one of Colorado's most difficult 14ers with sustained Class 4 climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: Little Bear is one of the most difficult standard 14er routes in Colorado. The Class 4 climbing is sustained and the rock quality is variable. Helmet is mandatory. A rope is recommended. Only for experienced alpine climbers.

tips.content: Camp at Lake Como for an early start on this demanding and long route.
Study the route carefully beforehand; route finding is the key to a safe ascent.
A 30m rope and light rack are recommended for the most exposed sections.

gear.notes: Absolutely mandatory for loose rock
Strongly recommended for the Class 4 sections
For overnight at Lake Como

reviews.title: A true test piece
reviews.body: Little Bear is everything they say it is. The Class 4 climbing is sustained, the rock is variable, and route finding is critical. One of the proudest summits on my 14er list.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cold, predawn start from Lake Como, late July

reviews.title: Difficult and dangerous
reviews.body: Little Bear is objectively dangerous. The rock is loose in places and the route finding is complex. But for experienced climbers, it is a worthy challenge. Do not attempt without solid alpine skills.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, light wind, early August

routes.name: Hourglass Couloir
routes.description: The Hourglass Couloir is a prominent feature on the west face of Little Bear Peak that provides an alternate route to the summit. This steep couloir narrows at its midpoint, creating the hourglass shape. The route involves Class 4 climbing on loose rock and is extremely dangerous due to constant rockfall funneled through the narrow couloir.
routes.summary: Extremely dangerous couloir route with severe rockfall hazard in the narrow hourglass.
routes.safetyNotes: The Hourglass funnels all rockfall through a narrow constriction, making it extremely dangerous. Multiple injuries and fatalities have occurred here. Only attempt in early morning when the rock is most stable. Helmet is absolutely mandatory.

tips.content: The Hourglass is best climbed before dawn when rock is frozen in place, reducing rockfall.
Do not climb this route if any other parties are above you in the couloir.

gear.notes: Absolutely critical for the severe rockfall danger
Couloir can hold snow and ice early season

reviews.title: Terrifying but direct
reviews.body: The Hourglass is objectively one of the most dangerous routes on any Colorado 14er. Rockfall is constant once the sun hits. We climbed in the dark and were off before sunrise. Not recommended.
reviews.conditions: Predawn, cold, frozen rock, early July

routes.name: West Approach from Fourmile Creek
routes.description: The standard route on Mount Sherman follows old mining roads and trails from the Fourmile Creek area. The route passes historic mining ruins before climbing moderate slopes to the summit. Sherman is one of the easiest 14ers in Colorado and is an excellent choice for beginners.
routes.summary: Easy route past historic mining ruins, excellent for beginners.
routes.safetyNotes: Stay away from old mine shafts and abandoned mining structures. The area has many hidden hazards from historic mining activity. Standard lightning precautions apply.

tips.content: This is one of the easiest 14ers in Colorado and excellent for beginners.
The historic mining ruins along the route add interesting historical context.
Stay away from old mine shafts and unstable structures along the route.

gear.notes: Exposed summit with afternoon storm potential
Helpful but not necessary on moderate terrain
Above treeline with minimal shade

reviews.title: Perfect easy 14er
reviews.body: Sherman is ideal for those new to 14ers. Short, moderate, and with interesting mining history along the way. The summit views are surprisingly good.

reviews.title: Easy with historic charm
reviews.body: The mining ruins add character to what would otherwise be a simple hike. One of the easiest 14ers but still a rewarding summit.

routes.name: Silver Creek Trail (Sunshine Combo)
routes.description: The standard route on Redcloud Peak follows the Silver Creek Trail from the trailhead on Cinnamon Pass road. This route is almost always combined with neighboring Sunshine Peak for a rewarding two-summit day. The trail is well-maintained and the terrain is moderate, making this one of the easier San Juan combos.
routes.summary: Well-maintained trail almost always combined with Sunshine Peak for two summits.
routes.safetyNotes: The Silver Creek crossing can be tricky during high water. The ridge between Redcloud and Sunshine is exposed to weather. Start early for the long day.

tips.content: Combine with Sunshine Peak for one of the best two-peak days in the San Juans.
Summit Redcloud first then traverse to Sunshine for the most efficient route.
The Cinnamon Pass road to the trailhead requires high clearance.

reviews.title: Classic San Juan two-peak day
reviews.body: Redcloud and Sunshine make a perfect pair. The trail is well-maintained and the traverse between them is scenic. Two beautiful summits in one moderate day.

reviews.title: Great combo hike
reviews.body: The Redcloud-Sunshine combo is one of the most efficient ways to bag two 14ers. Both peaks have excellent views. The stream crossing was a bit challenging in early July.

routes.name: Northeast Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Pyramid Peak ascends the northeast ridge from the Maroon Lake area. Pyramid is one of the most visually striking and technically challenging 14ers in Colorado. The route involves sustained Class 4 climbing on the Maroon Formation rock, which is notoriously loose. The steep approach and technical climbing make this a serious undertaking.
routes.summary: Technically demanding route on a visually striking peak with sustained Class 4 climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: Pyramid has the same terrible Maroon Formation rock as the nearby Maroon Bells. The Class 4 climbing is sustained and serious. Helmet is mandatory. Small party size recommended to minimize rockfall danger.

tips.content: The Maroon Formation rock on Pyramid is notoriously loose; test every hold.
Start very early to minimize rockfall as the sun warms the rock.
The green band of solid rock about two-thirds up the route provides a brief respite.

gear.notes: Absolutely mandatory for the loose Maroon Formation rock
Protects hands during sustained scrambling
Route finding is important on the upper mountain

reviews.title: Most beautiful 14er from below
reviews.body: Pyramid is perhaps the most photogenic 14er in Colorado. The climb is serious with terrible rock, but the summit is incredibly rewarding. A proud achievement for any climber.
reviews.conditions: Clear, cold, predawn start, late July

reviews.title: Respect the rock
reviews.body: Pyramid demands respect. The Maroon Formation is truly awful rock. But the climb is thrilling and the summit views of the Maroon Bells and Elk Range are world-class.
reviews.conditions: Clear, calm, early morning, early August

routes.name: Amphitheater Headwall
routes.description: An alternate approach to Pyramid Peak via the amphitheater headwall on the west side. This route is less traveled than the northeast ridge and involves steep Class 4 climbing in the headwall. The rock quality is similar to the rest of Pyramid. This route is for experienced alpine climbers seeking a different challenge.
routes.summary: Less-traveled alternate route via the western headwall with steep Class 4 climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: Same loose rock hazards as the NE ridge. The headwall is steep and committing. Route finding is critical. Only for experienced alpine climbers.

tips.content: This route sees very few climbers; don't expect to find others for help.
Route finding through the headwall is complex; study the route thoroughly beforehand.

gear.notes: Mandatory for the loose Maroon Formation rock
Recommended for the steepest headwall sections

reviews.title: Seldom-climbed and serious
reviews.body: The amphitheater headwall is even more remote and committing than the standard NE ridge. Rock is equally terrible. For those seeking adventure beyond the normal route.

routes.name: West Ridge from Rock of Ages
routes.description: The standard route on Wilson Peak (not to be confused with Mount Wilson) ascends the west ridge from the Rock of Ages area. The route involves Class 4 climbing near the summit with some exposure. Wilson Peak is famous for being the mountain depicted on the Coors beer label.
routes.summary: Standard route on the peak featured on the Coors label with Class 4 summit climbing.
routes.safetyNotes: The Class 4 sections near the summit require solid scrambling skills. Helmet recommended. The west ridge has some exposure.

tips.content: Wilson Peak is the mountain on the Coors beer label; bring a can for a summit photo.
The Silver Pick road to the trailhead requires high clearance 4WD.
The Class 4 sections are short but require careful climbing.

gear.notes: Recommended for loose rock near the summit
Helpful for the Class 4 scrambling
San Juan storms can develop rapidly

reviews.title: The Coors peak
reviews.body: Wilson Peak is a fun climb with exciting Class 4 near the summit. The views of the Wilson Group and Lizard Head are incredible. Brought a Coors for the obligatory summit photo.

reviews.title: Classic San Juan scramble
reviews.body: Wilson Peak delivers a great mountain experience. The Class 4 sections are fun and the summit views are outstanding. The approach road is rough.

routes.name: Silver Pick Approach
routes.description: An alternate approach to Wilson Peak from the Silver Pick Basin that avoids the most technical Class 4 sections by taking a slightly different line on the upper mountain. This route is still demanding with Class 3 scrambling but is less exposed than the standard west ridge.
routes.summary: Less technical alternate from Silver Pick Basin with Class 3 scrambling.
routes.safetyNotes: Less technical than the west ridge but still involves Class 3 scrambling. Route finding above treeline requires attention.

tips.content: This approach avoids the hardest Class 4 sections of the standard west ridge route.
Silver Pick Basin is accessed via the same road system as the Wilson Group.

gear.notes: Loose rock on the upper mountain
Helpful for route finding above treeline

reviews.title: Good alternative to the west ridge
reviews.body: This approach avoids the most exposed Class 4 on the west ridge. Still good scrambling but felt more comfortable. Silver Pick Basin is a beautiful area.

routes.name: East Ridge
routes.description: The standard route on Wetterhorn Peak ascends the east ridge from the Matterhorn Creek trailhead. The route is a pleasant hike to the base of the summit pyramid, where Class 3 scrambling leads to the dramatic pointed summit. The final scramble is exciting and exposed but short.
routes.summary: Hiking approach with a dramatic Class 3 scramble up the pointed summit pyramid.
routes.safetyNotes: The summit pyramid has some exposure and loose rock. The Class 3 scrambling is concentrated in a short section. Helmet recommended for the final push.

tips.content: The approach is a moderate hike; the excitement comes in the final summit scramble.
The Matterhorn Creek road to the trailhead requires high clearance.
The summit is a dramatic pointed top with great views of the San Juans.

gear.notes: Recommended for loose rock on the summit pyramid
Helpful for the Class 3 scrambling
Exposed summit with afternoon storm potential

reviews.title: Dramatic summit finish
reviews.body: Wetterhorn is a fun peak. The approach is an easy hike but the summit scramble is exciting and dramatic. The pointed top feels like a real mountaineering summit.

reviews.title: Fun Class 3 peak
reviews.body: The summit pyramid is a blast. Short but exciting Class 3 with some exposure. The approach hike is pleasant and the views from the top are excellent.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, light wind, late July

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.description: An alternate route ascending Wetterhorn via the southeast ridge. This route offers a different approach angle and slightly different scrambling than the standard east ridge. The upper mountain still involves the same dramatic summit pyramid. Less traveled than the standard route.
routes.summary: Less-traveled alternate approach via the southeast ridge to the summit pyramid.
routes.safetyNotes: Similar hazards to the east ridge route. Less traveled so trail markings may be sparse.

tips.content: This route sees fewer climbers for a more solitary experience.
The final summit pyramid is the same dramatic scramble regardless of approach.

gear.notes: For the summit pyramid scramble
Trail less defined than the standard route

reviews.title: Quieter approach to a great summit
reviews.body: The SE ridge sees fewer people. The approach is slightly longer but the summit scramble is the same exciting finish. Good option for those seeking more solitude.

routes.name: Stewart Creek Approach
routes.description: San Luis Peak is the most remote 14er in Colorado and the easiest by terrain. The standard route follows the Stewart Creek trail through gentle terrain to the broad, rounded summit. The route is entirely on trail and the grade is very moderate. The challenge is the remoteness and the long drive to the trailhead.
routes.summary: Most remote and easiest Colorado 14er with gentle terrain throughout.
routes.safetyNotes: The remoteness is the main concern. Cell service is nonexistent. The terrain is easy but the long drive and remote trailhead mean help is far away if needed.

tips.content: San Luis is the most remote 14er in Colorado; plan for a long drive to the trailhead.
Despite being easy terrain, bring proper gear as you are very far from help.
The gentle terrain and moderate grade make this a pleasant long hike.

gear.notes: Helpful for the long distance
Remote location with long approach
Help is very far away in this remote area

reviews.title: Peaceful and remote
reviews.body: San Luis is the antithesis of crowded Front Range 14ers. Long drive, long hike, but pure solitude. The easiest terrain of any 14er but the remoteness adds its own challenge.

reviews.title: Easy but very remote
reviews.body: The hike itself is unremarkable terrain-wise but the remote setting is beautiful. Plan for a very long day with the drive included. Barely saw another person.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, light wind, early August

routes.name: Redcloud-Sunshine Combo
routes.description: Sunshine Peak is almost always climbed in combination with Redcloud Peak from the Silver Creek trailhead. After summiting Redcloud, climbers traverse the connecting ridge south to Sunshine Peak before descending. The route is moderate Class 2 throughout and provides a very efficient two-peak day in the San Juans.
routes.summary: Almost always climbed as a combo with Redcloud via a scenic ridge traverse.
routes.safetyNotes: The connecting ridge is exposed to weather. Extended time above treeline. Watch for storms on the long traverse.

tips.content: Summit Redcloud first, then traverse to Sunshine for the most efficient outing.
The ridge between Redcloud and Sunshine is scenic but exposed to weather.
Bring extra food for the extended day at altitude.

gear.notes: Ridge between peaks is often windy
Helpful for the long day
Long day above treeline with no water

reviews.title: Great companion to Redcloud
reviews.body: Sunshine and Redcloud are a natural pair. The traverse is easy and scenic. Sunshine has a rockier summit area than Redcloud but the views are equally good.

reviews.title: Efficient two-peak day
reviews.body: The Redcloud-Sunshine combo is one of the most efficient in Colorado. Both peaks are rewarding and the connecting ridge is enjoyable.
reviews.conditions: Partly cloudy, moderate wind, late July

routes.name: North Ridge from Half Moon Pass
routes.description: The standard route on Mount of the Holy Cross ascends the north ridge from Half Moon Pass. The approach involves a steep descent into the Cross Creek drainage before climbing to the pass and then up the ridge. The famous cross-shaped snowfield is best seen from Notch Mountain across the valley. The route is physically demanding due to the significant elevation loss and regain.
routes.summary: Demanding standard route with significant elevation loss on approach to the famous cross peak.
routes.safetyNotes: The approach involves descending to Cross Creek and regaining that elevation on the return. This adds significant physical demand. The stream crossing can be tricky during high water. Budget extra time for the return climb.

tips.content: Be prepared for the demoralizing descent on the approach knowing you must climb it again on return.
The famous cross-shaped snowfield is best seen from Notch Mountain, not from the climbing route.
Some parties camp at the base to split the demanding approach into two days.

gear.notes: Essential for the steep approach descent and return climb
Stream crossings on the approach
Very demanding day with significant elevation changes

reviews.title: Tougher than expected
reviews.body: The approach with its descent and regain makes Holy Cross harder than the Class 2 rating suggests. The mountain itself is beautiful and historic. Plan for a very long day.

reviews.title: Historic peak with character
reviews.body: Mount of the Holy Cross has a special place in Colorado mountaineering history. The route is demanding but rewarding. The return climb from Cross Creek is a gut check.
reviews.conditions: Clear morning, afternoon clouds, late July

routes.name: West Slopes from South Winfield
routes.description: The standard route on Huron Peak ascends the west slopes from the ghost town of South Winfield. The trail climbs through forest and past mining ruins before ascending open alpine slopes to the summit. Huron is one of the more straightforward Sawatch Range 14ers with a moderate approach and good trail.
routes.summary: Standard route from the historic ghost town of South Winfield with moderate terrain.
routes.safetyNotes: The road to South Winfield requires high clearance. Standard 14er hazards apply. The upper slopes are exposed to weather.

tips.content: The ghost town of South Winfield at the trailhead has interesting historic mining structures.
The road to the trailhead requires high clearance; plan accordingly.
Huron has one of the shorter approaches in the Sawatch Range.

gear.notes: Afternoon storms common in the Sawatch
Helpful on the descent
Above treeline for the upper half

reviews.title: Charming peak with history
reviews.body: Huron is a straightforward and enjoyable 14er. The ghost town at the trailhead adds character. Good trail with moderate terrain and great summit views.

reviews.title: Solid Sawatch hike
reviews.body: One of the shorter and more moderate Sawatch peaks. The trail is in good shape and the views from the summit are excellent. The mining ruins on the approach are interesting.
